spec.section: # CHD-3.4 policy, readiness, archive and maintenance author evidence

## Scope and authority
This evidence records the CHD-3.4 authoring corrections in the five revised source sections and the new maintenance section. The selected authority is the integrated CHD-3.4 package, not a historical projection. No render was run and no runtime service, native Hermes adapter, or storage substrate was exercised.
Read sources:
- `audit/astra-audit.md`, especially G-02, G-06, G-07, G-08, G-09 and G-12; - `build-spec/INTEGRATION.md`, especially §§1–2 (D-038/D-039, readiness, capacity, fencing and unresolved native/storage gates); - `build-spec/integrated/config-format.md`, especially §§1.1–1.2, §§2.1–2.2, §§4.2–5.3 and §§5.4–6 (explicit inputs, unset defaults, readiness modes, capacity, fork choices and restore policy).

## Changed subsections and semantic disposition
| File | Changed subsection(s) | CHD-3.4 semantic correction | |---|---|---| | `src/30-provisioning-lifecycle.md` | revision/status header; D.7 Readiness gates; D.15 Dispatchable manager readiness route; new D.16 Release-gated native and fencing capabilities | Replaced one global readiness result with read-only, immediate and scheduled capability results. Scheduler outage blocks scheduled readiness only unless scheduler-owner admission is selected. Immediate dispatch requires authoritative attempt/run reservation, storage fencing and snapshot support. Native export/import and storage boundary remain explicit unresolved release gates. | | `src/60-authorization.md` | revision header; I.6.2 Restore is not a fork | Restore/replacement always resolves current policy before activation. Archived policy is history only. `source_policy_rev` is nullable when genuinely absent and carries a reason; it is never inferred. Fork default remains preserve-parent; current-policy is an explicit authorized choice; no ordered strictness or automatic live resync is introduced. | | `src/90-recovery.md` | revision/status header; N.2 Startup sequence and readiness gates; N.4 Reconciliation and capacity safety; N.7 Dependency outages; N.8 Backup, upgrade and restore; N.10.1 Startup gate and authority uncertainty | Scheduler readback is no longer a universal block. Report-only, waiting, timeout, cancellation, process absence and lease expiry cannot release capacity. Capacity belongs to the correlated authoritative attempt/run reservation and execution generation. Native archive and storage-fence uncertainty remains visible and blocking for the affected capability. | | `src/110-archives-restore.md` | status header; L.3 Native export envelope and immutable upload; L.5 Replacement discovery and validated import | Required native `hermes.session.export` support remains visible as OPEN-ARCHIVE-1. No native API/version, payload format, or transport is guessed. Restore uses a new identity and current policy; source revision is nullable with a verified absence reason. | | `src/120-deployment-federation.md` | revision/status header; new M.0 Deployment readiness contract; new M.0.1 Native and storage release gates | Federation/project memory cannot create a second capacity ledger or fencing authority. Read-only/immediate/scheduled readiness is separated. Scheduler outage does not globally block controller-local immediate service. Native adapter and storage boundary gates remain explicit. | | `src/210-maintenance.md` | new U.1–U.8 | Added real install/enroll, staged upgrade, rollback, controller backup, isolated restore drill, retention/tombstone, stop/retire and reconciliation procedures. Each includes preconditions, ordered effects, failure guards, idempotency, evidence, capacity handling and readback. The text does not substitute pointers or report-only proof. |

## Figure and illustration replacement register
The edited files contain no numbered `FIGURE` blocks. The following inherited semantic figure identifiers are referenced and must be replaced or re-captioned by the build/integration owner because their diagrams encode the changed readiness, capacity, or federation boundaries:
| Existing identifier | Required new semantic content | |---|---| | `fig-recovery.svg` / `fig-recovery.mmd` | Show capability-vector readiness; scheduler outage leaves read-only and controller-local immediate paths distinct from scheduled readiness. Show attempt/run reservation held through unknown and released only after authoritative stop proof. | | `fig-storage-topology.svg` and Mermaid source | Show LeaseAuthority/FencedStore/SnapshotToken as unresolved selected storage-boundary gates; no second SQLite/project-memory ledger; immediate and scheduled readiness depend on verified fence/snapshot. | | `fig-crier-bridge.svg` and Mermaid source | Preserve inbound/outbound federation separation and add that bridge/project-memory ACKs do not authorize work or release attempt/run capacity. |
These are semantic replacement requirements, not claims that a rendering was performed. No new figure ID is fabricated in this authoring pass.

## Required unresolved release gates
- **OPEN-ARCHIVE-1:** native Hermes export/import adapter capability, supported name/version, typed request/response/error contract, response-loss reconciliation, retention decision and executable export → import → first-turn trace. - **G-12 storage boundary:** versioned or explicitly owned LeaseAuthority, FencedStore and SnapshotToken binding, atomic reservation/fence semantics, stale-writer rejection at the write boundary, durable high-water reads and multi-page snapshot consistency. - **Stop producer:** authoritative attempt/run terminal status or trusted runtime stop attestation, correlated to send/attempt/run/execution generation. A normal report is not sufficient.

## Verification boundary
Textual post-edit checks were performed by reading the changed files and searching for the contradictory scheduler/global-ready, report-only stop, archived-policy activation, fabricated source-revision, and blanket temporary-worker-default claims. The maintenance file was written and verified by the file tool. No PDF or visual render was run as requested. This evidence records authoring/specification changes; it does not claim runtime implementation, live readiness, native archive capability, storage linearizability, stop attestation, or owner acceptance.
